unresolved.first_comment: **Different component keys collide** Distinct valid `_state_key` values can produce the same state name. For example, `cart_item` and `cartItem` pass this exact-name check, but `default_state_name` converts both generated class names to snake case. With minification off—the default—the second `create()` raises the sibling-shadowing error and stops app compilation. Check uniqueness using the final state name, or encode keys without losing their spelling. Note: If this suggestion doesn't match your team's coding style, reply to this and let me know. I'll remember it for next time!

P2: This check compares only the leaf of each function’s `__qualname__`, so distinct same-named handlers from different modules or nested scopes bypass it and the later handler overwrites the first. Compare the module plus full qualname before replacing the registry entry.

**Inspection misses separate state roots** `minify list` and `minify lookup` only walk the framework `State` tree, while `init`, `sync`, and `validate` cover every registered root. An app using an independent `BaseState` root, such as the existing `App(_state=Base)` test, therefore gets IDs that these inspection commands cannot show or resolve. Use the same root inventory across the commands so developers can inspect all IDs the CLI assigns.

P2: This conversion reintroduces numeric aliasing while allocating new state IDs: a valid sibling ID `"aa"` reserves the unrelated wire ID `"a"`. Preserve raw IDs through the allocation check, or ignore noncanonical aliases when building numeric reservations, so sync can assign the free `"a"` slot.
